product.name: Hold
product.tagline: Your baby's own pattern, built one tap at a time
product.dek: Hold is a companion for the third trimester: log a movement in one tap, watch your baby's own pattern build over the days, and when labour starts, time contractions with 5-1-1 guidance. It runs on your phone, and it works with the screen off just as well as on.
product.note: Below is what a pregnant parent actually meets, step by step — log a movement, watch the pattern build, and get ready for labour.

videoNote: Internal: GitHub Release assets only. See docs/DEMO-VIDEOS.md. Recorded from a seeded demo build — Ofcom drama-range numbers on screen, nothing dials a real person.

parts.kicker: Every day, from the third trimester
parts.title: Log a movement in one tap
parts.dek: No form, no timer to start. Feel something, tap the button, get on with your day — or sit down for a few minutes and let Hold time a proper count.

features.title: One tap, any time
features.summary: The big button on the Today tab logs that you felt a movement, right now. Nothing is debounced here — two felt movements are two taps, even a second apart. Say what you were doing afterwards if you want to; Hold never asks first.

features.title: A proper count: ten movements
features.summary: Sit down at a time your baby is usually active and log each movement as you feel it. Hold times how long the ten takes — not against a universal target, but against your own history, so a change is the thing to notice.

parts.title: A pattern only your baby could have
parts.dek: Hold will not name a usual time of day from a handful of taps — that would teach you the wrong normal. It waits for real evidence, and shows its working the whole way there.

features.title: Nothing to say yet
features.summary: Open the Pattern tab before logging anything and the card is already there, already carrying its own caveat — “Still learning the pattern” — and states plainly what it's waiting for: at least 20 movements across at least 3 days.

features.title: Real data, not a rhythm yet
features.summary: Two days in, the bars have height and the counts are real — but Hold still won't name a busiest time. Two days isn't a rhythm, and naming one here would be a guess dressed up as a fact.

features.title: The pattern speaks for the first time
features.summary: The moment Hold crosses its own threshold, the card changes from “still learning” to a claim — “usually active in the evening” — with the clock range and the context that keeps turning up, phrased as what you logged, never as a cause.

features.title: Pattern established, with context
features.summary: Two weeks of logging later, the same card is built on 188 movements instead of 59 — same shape, sturdier evidence. This is the view the feature exists for: your baby's own rhythm, in one glance.

features.title: A card built to share
features.summary: Screenshot the card, or tap Share — it exports as an image carrying the week and the caveat with it, so a partner or midwife gets the whole picture in one message, not a screenshot missing the context underneath.

parts.title: When labour comes
parts.dek: Labor Mode doesn't exist before term, and it isn't hidden behind a menu once it does — the app changes with you.

features.title: The transition at 37 weeks
features.summary: The same Today screen, now reading 37 weeks, 0 days. Nothing else has changed — until you scroll.

features.title: The invitation into Labor Mode
features.summary: Pinned lower on that same screen, and nowhere earlier: before 37+0 this banner doesn't exist, so Hold never suggests timing contractions to someone who is thirty weeks along.

features.title: Timing a contraction
features.summary: Strict dark theme regardless of your phone's own setting, because this screen gets read at 3am. Start and stop by hand; the last ten contractions list their lengths and the time between them.

features.title: 5-1-1 met — time to call
features.summary: An hour of contractions about five minutes apart and about a minute long satisfies the rule: the banner turns red, all three checks tick, and one tap dials your saved triage number.

parts.title: Calm, and everything for your midwife
parts.dek: The parts of the app that aren't about counting anything.

features.title: Calm
features.summary: Paced breathing — box breathing or 4-7-8 — with a circle to follow, one steadying line a day, and freeform notes. The copy here reassures about you, not the baby.

features.title: Care team, and a report for your midwife
features.summary: Dates, the care-team numbers with tap-to-call, and a PDF report — last 4 hours or last 7 days — built on your phone and shared through the normal share sheet. Reporting a pregnancy loss here deletes everything immediately and stops the app asking anything else.

parts.title: The whole third trimester, in one clip
parts.dek: An almost-empty log at week 28, the pattern refusing to speak and then speaking, the transition at term, and Labor Mode with 5-1-1 firing.

features.title: The full journey
features.summary: Week 28 through to labour: taps accumulating, the two evidence gates being crossed, the 37-week transition, and a contraction pattern that meets 5-1-1.

privacyParagraphs: No account needed — Hold works fully without one. If you choose to sign in with a TinyKite account, only your email identifies you to us; your pregnancy data (movements, contractions, notes) stays on your phone and is never uploaded.
Every tap, every counting session, every contraction is stored in a database on your device, not on our servers. There's no cloud sync, no ads, and no analytics reading over your shoulder.
The PDF report for your midwife is built on your phone and only leaves it when you choose to share or print it — through your phone's own share sheet, the same way you'd share a photo.
Reporting a pregnancy loss in Settings deletes everything Hold has recorded from your phone immediately, and the app stops asking you anything else.
trust.medicalHeading: Hold is not a medical device
medicalParagraphs: Hold never diagnoses. It records what you tell it and compares it against published guidance and your own history — nothing more.

There is no set number of movements that counts as normal. What matters is your baby's own pattern, and any change to it. If a count is taking longer than usual, or your baby's movements have slowed, stopped or changed, Hold's answer is always the same: contact your midwife or maternity unit — don't wait to see if things settle.

The 5-1-1 guide it uses for contractions — about five minutes apart, about a minute long, kept up for about an hour — is standard patient-facing guidance, not a threshold Hold invented. Meeting it, or feeling worried before you do, both mean the same thing: call.

closing.heading: Built for the person who just wants to know
closing.body: No universal number, no diagnosis, no account required — just your baby's own pattern, timed on your own phone, and a plan for when labour starts.
